Accepted safeguard revision from Jack Heart, 2026-11-04: best-effort shutdown is OK. He asks that the design account for existing guardian processes. This supersedes any stronger absolute deadline/cost guarantee inferred from the original brief and resolves the recorded blocker. RunPod/Vast already use best-effort self-scoped guardians with preboot and API-outage gaps. For Lium retain initial termination_hours, promptly acknowledged exact scheduled removal, controller reconciliation/removal retries and a local deadline/watchdog where feasible; reuse shared bootstrap/guardian machinery where compatible. Do not send a broad account credential to rented jobs. If no safe pod-scoped deletion authority exists, provider timer plus controller removal is acceptable with the distinction documented. A provider key spending cap is optional defense in depth, not an implementation/publication prerequisite or authority to change account settings. Preserve allocation admission/accounting and the existing USD10 TLA total; no deliberately enlarged spending is authorized. Continue implementation and authorized automatic delivery now.

Jack Heart narrowed the request on 2026-11-04: skip TensorDock; add ONLY Lium. This supersedes the original two-provider brief. Do not create a TensorDock follow-up Task. Deliver one Lium provider PR in loopflowstudio/etude through the existing authorized automatic delivery flow, building on EXP-35 / PR79 Vast support and the released etude-sdk0.2.14. Related consumer is MTG-213 (loopflow://manabot/task/MTG-213), whose prepared TLA run is blocked on compatible GPU supply.

Outcome: explicitly select Lium using the existing public Python/CLI provider and MachineTemplate interface. Availability, complete quotes, creation, bootstrap, execution, status, retrieval, deadlines, termination and accounting must use existing Etude owners. Preserve RunPod, Vast and owned-machine behavior. Do not add a competing scheduler, automatic provider fallback or change frozen worker environments. Integrate current main; the filing checkout predates delivered Vast support.

Acceptance:

* Verify current official APIs and validate typed provider facts. Unknown stock is not empty stock. Quote actual GPU count and allocated CPU/RAM/disk, including mandatory storage/transfer costs, then revalidate at creation. Keep spot distinct; the initial training path uses non-spot service.
* Lium public node CPU/RAM/disk values describe the WHOLE node; partial GPU rentals receive a share. Respect min_rentable_gpu_count, price_per_gpu_hour versus price_per_node_hour, and actual allocated resources. Do not imply a one-GPU rental includes the whole host.
* Map pods into the existing machine/rental lifecycle. Use layered best-effort deadline and spending protection through failed bootstrap, disconnects, unknown create replies, partial evidence and termination; do not claim guaranteed provider deletion or exact final charges. Do not blindly retry creates. Retain source, attempts, cleanup and accounting evidence without claiming settlement before it is verified. Handle any remaining billable storage correctly.
* LIUM_API_KEY is saved and exact-readback verified in Doppler etude/prd at Jack Heart's request. Inject secrets without printing, persisting in job records or transmitting to arbitrary jobs. Do not create/fund accounts or alter account settings as a side effect.
* Add concise Python/CLI setup docs and controlled fixtures for pricing, availability/refusal, proportional resources, bootstrap, unknown-create recovery, deadlines, teardown and accounting. Exercise the public interfaces offline. Follow [AGENTS.md/TESTING.md:](<http://AGENTS.md/TESTING.md:>) uv, typed Python, no induced load, pytest/mypy/Ruff/CI. Live API reads are separate evidence from fixtures; do not claim paid lifecycle proof without actually observing it. No new compute budget is authorized by this Task; any paid proof must fit existing explicit authorization and a concrete capped allocation.
* Publish and ship after required checks under the standing automatic-delivery authorization. Report PR/merge separately from SDK release and TLA execution. Do not release the SDK or rebind/rerun MTG-213 as a side effect.

Research handoff: Lium public feed at 2026-11-04 21:19 UTC listed three single-GPU secure-tier RTX5090 nodes at USD0.75/hour with 110GB RAM,14-24CPU and >=756GB free disk. Example node89044090-3d31-4c5a-a388-0d0a30aef107 in Kazakhstan, reported reliability99.6. A single secure4090 at USD0.35/hour had32CPU/94GB RAM in Greece, node619bc3dc-49b6-4a1b-a262-d37d286b199c, reliability92.6. A single secure3090 at USD0.30/hour had16CPU/63GB RAM in Romania, node796f8f5c-da84-4be5-a083-596aa686c2c6, reliability98.7. These dated listings are not reservations or startup proof.

Official references: [https://docs.lium.io/intro](<https://docs.lium.io/intro>) ; [https://docs.lium.io/developers/public-nodes-feed.md](<https://docs.lium.io/developers/public-nodes-feed.md>) ; [https://lium.io/api/openapi.json](<https://lium.io/api/openapi.json>) ; [https://lium.io/pricing.json](<https://lium.io/pricing.json>) ; [https://lium.io/api/public/v1/nodes](<https://lium.io/api/public/v1/nodes>) . Verify authenticated deployment behavior in current official docs. Provider examples do not authorize account/billing actions.

Overlap inspected: no duplicate provider Task. PR59 changes worker/courier.py and output-delivery tests; PR56 changes [cli.py](<http://cli.py>), [experiment.py](<http://experiment.py>) and evaluation docs/tests; PR58 concerns reporting/tracking. Preserve their independent scope. Dependabot PR81/7 affect dependencies/lockfile. Existing EXP8/9/12/13/14/15/17 are separate work and are not absorbed here.
